- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- If recent price history shows strong upward momentum (last 5–7 days rising >2%), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above recent peak.  
- If model shows sharp downward spike followed by rebound, forecast often lags; add 1–2 days of lagged price correction.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period; apply 1–2% downward bias for first 7–10 days.  
- If sentiment history includes a single positive spike, model tends to overreact; dampen forecast by 2–5% for 3–5 days after spike.
